**Decision** Propose a small section-scoped JavaScript and markup patch. The bug is caused by global selectors and one-time `DOMContentLoaded` binding, so only the first section instance is wired and Theme Editor replacement does not rebind the new DOM. This is a code-review proposal only. No upload, publish, merchant setting change, or live-page change is authorized. **Observed Facts** - Two `compact-buy` section instances can exist on one product template. - Changing the second selector leaves that form’s hidden `name="id"` input unchanged. - After replacing the first section in Theme Editor, its selector no longer updates its hidden input. - Current Liquid uses repeated static IDs: - `label for="VariantSelect"` - `select id="VariantSelect"` - Current JS uses: - `document.querySelector('[data-variant-select]')` - `document.querySelector('[data-cart-variant]')` - binding only inside `DOMContentLoaded` - Existing smoke coverage only tested initial page load and one available variant. - `settings_data.json` has unrelated uncommitted merchant changes and should not be touched. **Source-Level Diagnosis** `document.querySelector` returns only the first matching element. With multiple section instances, the first selector and first hidden input are paired globally, leaving the second form unwired. The second failure is lifecycle-related: Theme Editor section replacement inserts fresh markup after `DOMContentLoaded` has already fired. The existing code never initializes replaced sections, so the new selector has no listener. The repeated `id="VariantSelect"` is also invalid for multiple instances and can break label association. It is not the direct cause of the hidden input bug, but it should be fixed in the same minimal patch using `section.id`. **Smallest Compatible Patch** `sections/compact-buy.liquid` ```liquid
``` `assets/compact-buy.js` ```js (() => { const sectionSelector = '[data-product-picker]'; function initCompactBuy(root = document) { const sections = root.matches?.(sectionSelector) ? [root] : Array.from(root.querySelectorAll(sectionSelector)); sections.forEach((section) => { const selector = section.querySelector('[data-variant-select]'); const variantInput = section.querySelector('[data-cart-variant]'); if (!selector || !variantInput || selector.dataset.compactBuyBound === 'true') { return; } selector.dataset.compactBuyBound = 'true'; selector.addEventListener('change', () => { variantInput.value = selector.value; }); }); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { initCompactBuy(document); }); document.addEventListener('shopify:section:load', (event) => { initCompactBuy(event.target); }); })(); ``` If the theme has a known section lifecycle helper, use that instead of directly listening to `shopify:section:load`. The core requirement is the same: initialize per section root, not globally. **Preservation Requirements** - Preserve standard Shopify product form behavior: - `form action="{{ routes.cart_add_url }}"` - `method="post"` - hidden input `name="id"` - Preserve existing translations: - `products.product.product_variants` - `products.product.add_to_cart` - Preserve variant availability behavior: - unavailable variants remain rendered as disabled options - selected/default variant remains `product.selected_or_first_available_variant` - Do not modify merchant settings, campaign data, product coverage, tracking, offers, or live theme state. - Do not touch unrelated `settings_data.json` changes. **Tests** Recommended focused tests: 1. Multiple sections on one product template: - Render two `compact-buy` sections. - Change the second select. - Assert only the second form’s hidden `name="id"` value changes. 2. First section still works: - Change the first select. - Assert the first form’s hidden input changes. 3. Section replacement lifecycle: - Simulate or trigger `shopify:section:load` with a newly inserted section root. - Change its select. - Assert its hidden input updates. 4. Duplicate binding guard: - Call initialization twice on the same section. - Change the select. - Assert behavior remains correct and no duplicated side effects occur. 5. Markup validity: - With two sections, verify each label `for` points to a unique select ID. Existing smoke coverage is insufficient because it only covers initial page load and one available variant. **Inferences** - The hidden input remains stale because the second section is never paired with its own selector. - Theme Editor replacement fails because new markup is inserted after the only initialization pass. - `section.id` is the smallest available stable value for making the select ID unique per section. **Unknowns** - How `assets/compact-buy.js` is loaded. - Whether the theme already has JavaScript section registration conventions. - Behavior for all-unavailable products. - Subscription or selling-plan product behavior. **Deployment State** Draft patch only. Target is unpublished preview theme `77102` on branch `fix/picker-review`. Live theme `77100` is unchanged. Uploading, publishing, and modifying merchant settings are not approved.
